facts.raw_span: a 1-year history of slow but progressive swelling near her gluteal cleft
denied fevers, chills, pain, drainage, bleeding, or rectal bleeding
a 4 × 4 cm area of swelling just left of the natal cleft at the level of the tip of the coccyx
mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin but no fluctuance, purulence, or visible pilonidal pits
no fluid was obtained
a complex and septated 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass was excised from the subcutaneous tissue near the coccyx
the mass was adherent to subcutaneous fat but did not involve the coccyx or anal sphincter
a high suspicion for abscess
the differential diagnosis at this time included inclusion cyst and soft-tissue tumor
percutaneous aspiration was performed in clinic
a 6-cm vertical incision was made over the lesion in the prone jack-knife position
the specimen was oriented with sutures and sent for permanent pathology

concepts.why: The patient presented with a swelling near the gluteal cleft, and the examination revealed a complex and septated mass, which is consistent with a pilonidal cyst.
The differential diagnosis included soft-tissue tumor, and the mass excised from the subcutaneous tissue near the coccyx could be consistent with a soft tissue tumor.
The differential diagnosis included inclusion cyst, and the mass excised from the subcutaneous tissue near the coccyx could be consistent with an inclusion cyst.
The patient had a high suspicion for abscess, and percutaneous aspiration was performed in clinic, although no fluid was obtained.
The patient presented with a swelling near the gluteal cleft, and the examination revealed a complex and septated mass, which could be consistent with an epidermoid cyst.
The mass was adherent to subcutaneous fat but did not involve the coccyx or anal sphincter, which is consistent with an epidermoid cyst.

rationales.F01: The patient's 1-year history of slow but progressive swelling near her gluteal cleft suggests a possible pilonidal cyst, inclusion cyst, or soft tissue tumor.
rationales.F02: The absence of fevers, chills, pain, drainage, bleeding, or rectal bleeding makes an abscess less likely.
rationales.F06: The complex and septated mass excised from the subcutaneous tissue near the coccyx is more consistent with a soft tissue tumor or inclusion cyst than a pilonidal cyst or abscess.

frontier_selector.rationale: The complex and septated mass with mild blanching erythema and no fluctuance or purulence, along with its location and adherence to subcutaneous fat, supports Epidermoid cyst as the most fitting diagnosis.
